raw_response:
I will do it close to how I have done in recent years, with small adjustments for cost and yield. On my 5 mu in Quzhou, the wheat-maize rotation is normal, and with well irrigation I do not want the crop to suffer for water or fertilizer. I finished middle school, so I do not just copy blindly, but I still start from what worked before and what nearby farmers are doing. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more fertilizer before sowing, then topdress nitrogen at jointing, and give about 3 irrigations if the year is normal. Wheat is sensitive if it goes hungry in spring, so I would rather not cut nitrogen too hard. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because the yield is steadier, put part of the fertilizer at planting and the rest before the big bell-mouth stage, and irrigate about 2 times if rainfall is not enough. On only 5 mu, every bag costs money, but losing yield costs more, so I will keep fertilizer and spray at a level that is common locally and reliable for my land.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation on all 5.0 mu and manage it in the way most steady local farmers do, because this system is proven here and I have well irrigation. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, apply a solid base fertilizer with enough nitrogen for spring growth, irrigate about three times, and spray twice to protect yield. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a little higher than wheat because maize responds well when water is available, irrigate around two times depending on rain, and spray twice. My farm is not large, so I must watch cost, but I will not save money by cutting fertilizer too much because one bad harvest hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs.
